newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips push Casablanca Bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips push Casablanca Bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Friday 0.82 percent higher, led by blue chips and notably by ONA holding, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 451.90 points from 448.23 points on Thursday. Over the week, the index rose 1.75 percent.
"I think people are anticipating good annual results for ONA group," said Magid Benjelloun, analyst at Casablanca-based Maroc Inter Titres.
ONA group jumped 20 dirhams to close at 541 dirhams. Wafabank, a liquid stock, which recently merged with Spanish Uniban bank, remained unchanged at 550 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur was up five dirhams to 405 dirhams.

"It is the only stock in the banking sector which has significantly risen after a long period of stagnation at 400 dirhams, but there is no real explanation for the rise," he added. Brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc gained 40 dirhams to trade at 1440 dirhams.
"The firm is expected to expand after it signed contracts with foreign investors," Benjelloun said.
Credit firm Eqdom Credit, which announced a capital increase recently, was up 22 dirhams to close at 762 dirhams.
Eqdom, Morocco's first consumer credit company, was set up in 1974 by holding company Societe Nationale d'Investissement and major insurance companies.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant in which Morocco plans to sell 31 percent to 51 percent to foreign investors, dropped one dirham to 243 dirham.
Credit firm Credor CRD.CS, which was recently introduced on the stock market, gained one dirham to 464 dirhams. Its initial price was 385 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest conglomerate, closed unchanged at 550 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 35.4 million dirhams from 10 million dirhams on Thursday.
